# Bookmuse

> Bookmuse is a book-summaries app for iPhone, iPad and Android: big ideas from great books, made visual. Each summary is a short course of interactive lessons (diagrams that move, guess-first questions, a quiz and the key takeaways) that teaches a book's core ideas in a few short sittings.

Bookmuse is free to download. One summary a day is free to read in full, the same one for everyone (it changes at 00:00 UTC); every other summary opens as a preview (the intro and the first three lessons). Bookmuse Pro, a monthly or yearly subscription in the App Store (the yearly plan starts with a 7-day free trial), opens every summary and adds 10 GB of cloud storage and more Bookmuse AI. Reading summaries needs a free account. The app needs iOS or iPadOS 26 and also runs on Apple-silicon Macs as the iPad app. Summaries are in English. It was made by Quan Ngo Van (wanngo).

## How a summary works

- An intro: the book's core idea in one or two sentences, a little about the author, and the list of lessons.
- Five to eight lessons, one big idea each, two or three minutes each. Lessons explain with short text, diagrams, charts and maps, animations, guess-first questions (answer before you are told), quick checks, small things to try (sliders, drag-to-explore charts) and everyday examples.
- A quiz that checks the ideas and explains the answers.
- The key takeaways on one screen.
- One lesson on screen at a time, with a bar that shows where you are; your place syncs across devices.
- Anyone can try a summary in a web browser from its share link; today's free summary is always at https://bookmuse-app.wanngo.com/s/today

## Books

- Popular non-fiction across self-growth, productivity, happiness, business and career, money and investing, leadership, negotiation, relationships, health, society and tech, personalities and spirituality, among others. New summaries are added every week.
- Shelves on Home: Free Today, Picked for You (from the interests you choose and what you read), Because you read…, collections, Popular, New and categories.
- Ratings and reviews from other readers on each summary.

## Lessons made by your AI

- Connect an AI agent (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Claude Code) to your Bookmuse library through the Bookmuse MCP server and ask it for a lesson on any topic. It adds an interactive HTML lesson to your Library, with its diagrams and quizzes working.
- Agents manage the person's own books, highlights, saved words and folders. They can't read summaries, post to the feed or make share links.

## Your own books, too

- Open DRM-free EPUB, PDF, Kindle (MOBI, AZW3), FB2, TXT and Markdown files, HTML notes and comics (CBZ, CBR) from Files, Google Drive, Dropbox or catalogs such as Project Gutenberg.
- Free on-device voices read them aloud in English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Vietnamese, Chinese and Japanese.
- Bookmuse AI explains a word in its sentence and answers questions about the page.
- A web dashboard at https://bookmuse-app.wanngo.com manages your own books from a computer: upload, edit details and covers, folders, download and delete.

## Summaries

Each summary has a public page with its free part (the intro and the first three lessons) at https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/<slug>/. All of them: https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/

- [Thinking, Fast and Slow](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/thinking-fast-and-slow/) by Daniel Kahneman: Your mind runs on a fast, automatic storyteller that feels sure and a slow, lazy checker that mostly signs off, so thinking better means learning the storyteller's tricks by name and slowing down when the stakes are high.
- [The Mountain Is You](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-mountain-is-you/) by Brianna Wiest: Self-sabotage is not a flaw. It is a way of coping that meets a need you cannot see, so you get free by finding the need, feeling what you avoid, and changing one small step at a time.
- [Can't Hurt Me](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/can-t-hurt-me/) by David Goggins: Most people quit long before their limit, and you can move that limit by telling yourself the truth, doing hard things on purpose and learning from every failure.
- [The Prince](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-prince/) by Niccolò Machiavelli: A ruler keeps power by judging people as they really are, relying on his own strength, never making his people hate him, and preparing in calm times for the day luck turns.
- [The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-monk-who-sold-his-ferrari/) by Robin Sharma: A fulfilling life is built from the inside: a trained mind, a clear purpose, daily self-improvement and a life of giving, lived now and not later.
- [Atomic Habits](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/atomic-habits/) by James Clear: Small habits, repeated every day, build the person you want to become. Make good habits obvious, attractive, easy and satisfying, and flip those four laws to break bad ones.
- [Ikigai](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/ikigai/) by Héctor García, Francesc Miralles: A long, happy life starts with a reason to get up each morning, kept alive by staying busy, close to friends, light on food, gentle in movement and calm in pace.
- [The Body Keeps the Score](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-body-keeps-the-score/) by Bessel van der Kolk: Trauma is not only what happened. It is the mark left on the brain and body, and healing means helping them feel safe in the present.
- [The Courage to Be Disliked](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-courage-to-be-disliked/) by Ichiro Kishimi, Fumitake Koga: People are not stuck because of their past. They are stuck because change feels scary, and the way out is the courage to live your own life, even if some people dislike you.
- [The Power of Habit](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-power-of-habit/) by Charles Duhigg: Habits are loops that run without thought, and once you know how a loop works, you can change it.
- [Boundaries](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/boundaries/) by Dr. Henry Cloud, Dr. John Townsend: A boundary is the property line of your life: it shows what you own and what is someone else’s, and setting it clearly lets you give a real yes and a real no instead of giving out of fear or guilt.
- [Cosmos](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/cosmos/) by Carl Sagan: We live on a small world in a vast and ancient Cosmos, we come from it, and science is how we found out.
- [Crucial Conversations](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/crucial-conversations-tools-for-talking-when-stakes-are-high/) by Joseph Grenny, Kerry Patterson, Ron McMillan, Al Switzler, Emily Gregory: Most problems last because we dodge or botch the talks that matter most, and the way out is to make it safe for everyone to say what they think, starting with your own motives and your own stories.
- [Ego Is the Enemy](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/ego-is-the-enemy/) by Ryan Holiday: Ego is an unhealthy belief in your own importance, and it works against you when you aim for a goal, when you reach it and when you fail. Humility and steady work are the cure.
- [Good Vibes, Good Life](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/good-vibes-good-life/) by Vex King: Vex King argues that loving yourself, which means accepting who you are while you keep growing, lifts your mood, and that your mood decides what comes back to you.
- [Grit](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/grit/) by Angela Duckworth: What you achieve over a lifetime depends more on grit than on talent. Grit is passion and perseverance for a goal that matters to you, and it can be grown.
- [How to Read a Book](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/how-to-read-a-book/) by Mortimer J. Adler: A hard book can lift your understanding, but only if you work on it: first to see its shape, then to grasp what it says, and last to judge it fairly.
- [Man’s Search for Meaning](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/man-s-search-for-meaning/) by Viktor E. Frankl: People are driven most by a search for meaning, not by pleasure or power, and a person with a reason to live can bear almost any hardship, because one freedom can never be taken away: the freedom to choose how to respond.
- [Nonviolent Communication](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/nonviolent-communication/) by Marshall B. Rosenberg: Judging and demanding make people defend themselves or give in out of fear. Saying what you see, feel, need and ask for, and hearing the same four things in others, lets people give from the heart.
- [The Four Agreements](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-four-agreements/) by Don Miguel Ruiz: As children we agreed to beliefs we never chose, and four new agreements can replace the ones that make us suffer.
- [The Intelligent Investor](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-intelligent-investor/) by Benjamin Graham, Jason Zweig: Treat a stock as a small piece of a real business: pay less than it is worth, plan for being wrong, and do not let the market’s moods or your own run your money.
- [Why Nations Fail](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/why-nations-fail/) by Daron Acemoglu and James A. Robinson: Nations are rich or poor because of their institutions, the rules that decide who can work, invest and hold power. Rules that share power make a country rich. Rules that let a few take from the many keep it poor.
- [Breaking the Habit of Being Yourself](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/breaking-the-habit-of-being-yourself/) by Joe Dispenza: To change your life, you must stop being the self you have memorized, then rehearse a new self until it feels real.
- [Getting Things Done](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/getting-things-done/) by David Allen: Your mind is "for having ideas, not for holding them", so get everything that has your attention out of your head, decide the next step on each thing, and review it all every week.
- [Guns, Germs, and Steel](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/guns-germs-and-steel/) by Jared Diamond: Peoples ended up with different power because of the land, plants and animals they started with, not because of any difference in their minds.
- [Men Are from Mars, Women Are from Venus](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/men-are-from-mars-women-are-from-venus/) by John Gray: Most clashes between a man and a woman come from forgetting they are different, and love lasts when each learns what the other needs.
- [Surrounded by Idiots](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/surrounded-by-idiots/) by Thomas Erikson: In Erikson's model, people act in four main styles, and you get through to anyone by meeting them on their terms, not yours.
- [The Magic of Thinking Big](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-magic-of-thinking-big/) by David J. Schwartz: How far you go depends on how big you think: believe you can, drop your excuses and act, and your results grow to match.
- [The Obstacle Is the Way](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-obstacle-is-the-way/) by Ryan Holiday: Whatever blocks your way can be used. See it clearly, act on it with energy, and accept what you cannot change, and the obstacle becomes the way forward.
- [Think Again](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/think-again/) by Adam Grant: Being smart is not enough: in a world that changes fast, rethinking and unlearning matter just as much, and you build them by thinking like a scientist.
- [A Brief History of Time](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/a-brief-history-of-time/) by Stephen Hawking: The universe runs on laws we can understand, and joining the science of the very big with the science of the very small may show how it all began.
- [Becoming Supernatural](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/becoming-supernatural/) by Joe Dispenza: Your thoughts, actions and feelings keep your future a copy of your past, and you can change them ahead of time with a clear intention and an elevated emotion, until your body believes the new life has begun.
- [Getting to Yes](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/getting-to-yes/) by Roger Fisher, William Ury, Bruce Patton: You do not have to choose between being hard and being soft. Settle the problem itself, not a contest of will, protect the person across the table, and look for a result both sides can call fair.
- [Mastery](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/mastery/) by Robert Greene: Mastery is not a gift some people are born with. It grows in anyone who finds the work that fits them, then spends years in three phases of learning, until they can feel their whole field at once.
- [Mindset](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/mindset/) by Carol S. Dweck: Your abilities can be carved in stone, or they can be grown. Which one you believe shapes how you handle challenge, failure and effort, and you can change it.
- [The Power of Positive Thinking](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-power-of-positive-thinking/) by Norman Vincent Peale: What you keep in your mind shapes how you feel and act, so push out fear and doubt, fill your mind with faith, and expect the best.
- [The Secret](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-secret/) by Rhonda Byrne: Your thoughts and feelings send out a signal, and the law of attraction brings back whatever matches it.
- [Zero to One](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/zero-to-one/) by Peter Thiel, Blake Masters: Copying what works takes the world from 1 to n; real progress is making something new, from 0 to 1.
- [101 Essays That Will Change The Way You Think](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/101-essays-that-will-change-the-way-you-think/) by Brianna Wiest: Your problem is rarely what happened. It is how you think about it, so a changed mind can change a life.
- [12 Rules for Life](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/12-rules-for-life/) by Jordan B. Peterson: Life is hard and full of chaos, and the best answer is to take responsibility for yourself: stand tall, care for yourself, tell the truth, and aim at something worth the cost.
- [Astrophysics for People in a Hurry](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/astrophysics-for-people-in-a-hurry/) by Neil deGrasse Tyson: The same laws of physics work everywhere, so by reading every kind of light we have traced the universe from a pinpoint to us, and most of it is still dark.
- [Principles for Dealing with the Changing World Order](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/principles-for-dealing-with-the-changing-world-order/) by Ray Dalio: Empires, their money and their markets rise and fall in one repeating Big Cycle, so the smart move is to learn its pattern and protect yourself from the worst case.
- [Shoe Dog](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/shoe-dog/) by Phil Knight: Phil Knight built Nike from a crazy idea. He did it by believing in it, by giving odd and driven people room to run with it, and by never stopping when money or partners let him down.
- [The Art of Loving](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-art-of-loving/) by Erich Fromm: Love is not a feeling that happens to you but a skill of giving, learned through knowledge and daily practice, and it needs a person who has grown up enough to care.
- [The Millionaire Next Door](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-millionaire-next-door/) by Thomas J. Stanley and William D. Danko: Most American millionaires are ordinary people who spend far less than they earn and invest the rest, while many high earners who look rich own little.
- [The Selfish Gene](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-selfish-gene/) by Richard Dawkins: Evolution works on genes, not on groups: genes that copy themselves well spread, bodies are the machines they build, and kindness shows up among relatives and between players who meet again.
- [The Simple Path to Wealth](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-simple-path-to-wealth/) by J.L. Collins: Spend less than you earn, avoid debt, and put the rest in one low-cost fund that owns the whole stock market. Then stay calm when it falls.
- [As a Man Thinketh](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/as-a-man-thinketh/) by James Allen: Your thoughts grow into your character, your circumstances and your health, so the way to change your life is to change what you think.
- [Don’t Believe Everything You Think](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/don-t-believe-everything-you-think-why-your-thinking-is-the-beginning-and-end-of-suffering/) by Joseph Nguyen: Joseph Nguyen says that events do not make you suffer, your thinking about them does, and when that thinking settles, peace is what is left.
- [Eat That Frog!](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/eat-that-frog/) by Brian Tracy: Start each day with your biggest, most important task, and stay on it until it is done.
- [Games People Play](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/games-people-play/) by Eric Berne: Much of what people do together is a game: a set of moves with a hidden message that ends in a predictable payoff. Spot the game, and you can stop playing it.
- [Playing to Win](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/playing-to-win/) by A.G. Lafley and Roger L. Martin: Strategy is not a vision or a plan. It is a set of five connected choices about how you will win, and you can test those choices by asking “What would have to be true?”
- [Quiet](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/quiet/) by Susan Cain: Our culture treats the bold, talkative style as the best one. Yet up to half of Americans are introverts, and quiet strengths are powers we cannot afford to waste.
- [The Laws of Human Nature](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-laws-of-human-nature/) by Robert Greene: Deep forces such as emotion, self-love, envy and fear drive us without our knowing, and once you see them in others and in yourself, you stop being caught off guard.
- [The Mind-Gut Connection](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-mind-gut-connection/) by Emeran Mayer: Your brain, your gut and the trillions of microbes in it talk to each other all day, and what you eat and how you feel changes what they say.
- [The Next Millionaire Next Door](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-next-millionaire-next-door/) by Thomas J. Stanley and Sarah Stanley Fallaw: People build wealth with everyday habits: they spend less than they earn, ignore what others show off, and run their money like a job.
- [The Science of Getting Rich](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-science-of-getting-rich/) by Wallace D. Wattles: Wallace D. Wattles claims that getting rich is an exact science: picture what you want, hold it with faith and thanks, and act well every day, and you will get rich.
- [The Untethered Soul](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-untethered-soul/) by Michael A. Singer: You are not your thoughts or your feelings. You are the one who notices them, and you grow free by letting them pass instead of guarding yourself.
- [Think Like a Monk](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/think-like-a-monk/) by Jay Shetty: You do not need robes or a monastery to find peace and purpose: you train your mind the way monks do, by letting go, growing and giving.
- [All About Love](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/all-about-love/) by bell hooks: Love is not a feeling that happens to us. It is a choice we make again and again, and we learn it by telling the truth, treating people fairly and facing our fear.
- [Capital in the 21st Century](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/capital-in-the-21st-century/) by Thomas Piketty: When wealth earns more each year than the economy grows, money from the past pulls ahead of pay from the present, and inequality rises unless people choose to act.
- [I Am Malala](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/i-am-malala/) by Malala Yousafzai, Christina Lamb: A girl who loved school kept speaking up for it when the Taliban banned it. They shot her for it, and her voice only grew louder.
- [Outwitting the Devil](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/outwitting-the-devil/) by Napoleon Hill: In this book the Devil is fear living in the unused part of your mind, and you outwit him by deciding what you want and thinking for yourself.
- [Psycho-Cybernetics](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/psycho-cybernetics-a-new-way-to-get-more-living-out-of-life/) by Maxwell Maltz, MD: Your mind steers you toward the picture you hold of yourself. Change that picture, with vivid imagination, calm practice and new habits, and you change what you do.
- [Steve Jobs](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/steve-jobs/) by Walter Isaacson: Steve Jobs made products people loved by joining art with technology, controlling the whole experience and keeping only what mattered, and the same intensity that drove the work often hurt the people around him.
- [The Personal MBA](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-personal-mba/) by Josh Kaufman: Every business is five simple parts, and you can learn them yourself, along with how people and systems behave, without an expensive degree.
- [Tuesdays with Morrie](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/tuesdays-with-morrie/) by Mitch Albom: Facing death honestly shows what matters in life: love, giving, attention and forgiveness, not money, status or hurry.
- [What If?](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/what-if-serious-scientific-answers-to-absurd-hypothetical-questions/) by Randall Munroe: A silly question, answered seriously with simple numbers, shows you how the world really works.
- [Who Moved My Cheese?](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/who-moved-my-cheese-an-amazing-way-to-deal-with-change-in-your-work-and-in-your-life/) by Spencer Johnson: Change always comes, and the fear in your own head holds you back more than the change does, so notice it early, let go of the old and move toward something better.
- [Women Who Love Too Much](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/women-who-love-too-much/) by Robin Norwood: Loving too much means obsessing about a man who cannot love you back and calling it love. The way out is to turn all that effort toward yourself.
- [Atlas Shrugged](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/atlas-shrugged/) by Ayn Rand: The world runs on the minds of people who think and build. Punish them for it, and they will leave, and everything stops with them.
- [Automate the Boring Stuff with Python](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/automate-the-boring-stuff-with-python-2nd-edition/) by Al Sweigart: A short program can do in seconds the repetitive computer jobs that eat your hours, and you do not have to be a software engineer to write one.
- [Being Mortal](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/being-mortal/) by Atul Gawande: When a body can no longer be fixed, safety and a longer life are not enough: people want to stay the authors of their own story, so doctors, care homes and families must ask what matters most and shape care around it.
- [Blink](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/blink/) by Malcolm Gladwell: Decisions made in the first two seconds can be as good as slow, careful ones, but they can be fooled, so learn when to trust a first impression, when to guard it and how to train it.
- [Born a Crime](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/born-a-crime/) by Trevor Noah: Apartheid made Trevor Noah’s birth a crime and tried to keep people apart, and a mother who loved hard, taught him to think and found the cracks in unjust rules gave him ways to cross every line.
- [Dare](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/dare/) by Barry McDonagh: Anxiety is a wave of nervous energy, and it traps you only when you fear it, so you heal by moving with the wave, not against it.
- [Eat & Run](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/eat-and-run/) by Scott Jurek, Steve Friedman: Strength to keep going is built by doing hard things one piece at a time, with good food, a calm mind and friends, and the journey matters more than the prize.
- [Educated](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/educated1/) by Tara Westover: Being educated means learning to weigh many voices and build your own mind, and for Tara Westover that cost her family.
- [Hinch Yourself Happy](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/hinch-yourself-happy/) by Mrs. Hinch: A home you love and look after can calm a worried mind, because cleaning gives your thoughts a job, a finish line and a small win.
- [I Want to Die but I Want to Eat Tteokbokki](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/i-want-to-die-but-i-want-to-eat-tteokbokki/) by Baek Sehee: Feeling low and wanting a good meal can live in one person, and a mind that thinks in extremes makes the hurt worse; a middle ground, taken one small step at a time, helps.
- [I’m Glad My Mom Died](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/im-glad-my-mom-died/) by Jennette McCurdy: A girl raised to live for her mother’s approval loses track of what she wants, and she begins to heal only when she tells the truth about her mother and learns what she wants herself.
- [Outliers](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/outliers/) by Malcolm Gladwell: Successful people did not rise on talent and hard work alone. Hidden chances, the year they were born and the culture they came from helped make them.
- [Salt, Sugar and Fat](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/salt-sugar-and-fat-how-the-food-giants-hooked-us/) by Michael Moss: Food companies build their products around salt, sugar and fat so that people want more, and they will not stop on their own.
- [Team of Teams](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/team-of-teams/) by Stanley McChrystal, Tantum Collins, David Silverman and Chris Fussell: A large organization built to be efficient will lose in a fast, tangled world, unless it learns to work as a team of teams: everyone sees the whole picture, and the people closest to a problem decide.
- [The Bhagavad Gita](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-bhagavad-gita/) by Vyasa: You are a deathless self, so do your duty with a steady mind, let go of the reward, and make God your refuge.
- [The Design of Everyday Things](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-design-of-everyday-things/) by Don Norman: When a thing is hard to use, the design failed, not you. Good design shows what to do, answers every action, and expects people to slip.
- [The Good Life](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-good-life-lessons-from-the-world-s-longest-scientific-study-of-happiness/) by Robert Waldinger and Marc Schulz: Good relationships keep us happier, healthier and alive longer, and it is never too late to build them.
- [The Lean Startup](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-lean-startup/) by Eric Ries: A startup exists to learn how to build a business that lasts, and it learns fastest by testing each guess with real customers in small steps.
- [The Omnivore's Dilemma](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-omnivores-dilemma/) by Michael Pollan: Most of what we eat comes from one cheap crop, corn, and its real cost is hidden. Knowing where your food comes from helps you choose better.
- [Turn the Ship Around!](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/turn-the-ship-around/) by L. David Marquet: In Marquet's account, people treated as followers act like followers; give them control, plus the competence and the clarity to use it, and they act like leaders.
- [When Breath Becomes Air](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/when-breath-becomes-air/) by Paul Kalanithi: Death comes for everyone, so the real question is how to live with it: with other people, with honesty, and by going on.
- [Women Who Run With the Wolves](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/women-who-run-with-the-wolves/) by Clarissa Pinkola Estés: Every woman has a wild, instinctive self that knows what is true and what she needs. Being trained to be tame buries it, and old stories show how to dig it up and live with it.
- [A People's History of the United States](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/a-people-s-history-of-the-united-states/) by Howard Zinn: Told from below, American history shows a few powerful people using the nation, the law and war to protect their wealth, and ordinary people who pushed back again and again and sometimes won.
- [A Room of One's Own](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/a-room-of-ones-own/) by Virginia Woolf: A woman needs money of her own and a room with a lock on the door if she is to write fiction, because a free mind needs both, and for centuries women had neither.
- [Elon Musk](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/elon-musk/) by Ashlee Vance: Elon Musk builds companies to solve problems he has cared about since he was young, and he gets there by learning fast, risking his own money and asking for the impossible.
- [Emotional Blackmail](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/emotional-blackmail/) by Susan Forward with Donna Frazier: Emotional blackmail is a threat from someone close: do what I want, or you will suffer. It works through fear, obligation and guilt, and it ends when you change how you respond.
- [Factfulness](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/factfulness-ten-reasons-we-re-wrong-about-the-world/) by Hans Rosling, Ola Rosling and Anna Rosling Rönnlund: Almost everyone sees the world as more frightening and hopeless than it is, because ten built-in instincts pull our thinking toward drama.
- [Freakonomics](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/freakonomics/) by Steven D. Levitt and Stephen J. Dubner: People respond to incentives, and when you follow the data, the popular story is often wrong.
- [Hillbilly Elegy](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/hillbilly-elegy/) by J.D. Vance: A poor town's troubles are not only about lost jobs. They also come from chaos at home and a belief that your choices do not matter, and one steady, loving person can change a child's life.
- [Invent & Wander](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/invent-and-wander/) by Jeff Bezos and Walter Isaacson: Bezos built Amazon by thinking in years, serving customers instead of rivals, and inventing through many bold bets, and he tried to keep it Day One as the company grew.
- [On Writing](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/on-writing/) by Stephen King: Writing is one mind reaching another, and hard work can make a competent writer good: read a lot, write a lot, use plain honest words, find the story, and cut your second draft.
- [The Art of Stillness](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-art-of-stillness/) by Pico Iyer: The world keeps speeding up, so one of the most useful things you can do is go nowhere on purpose: sit still often, and bring the calm back into your life.
- [The Fire Next Time](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-fire-next-time/) by James Baldwin: James Baldwin says America's race problem grows out of white fear and white innocence, that hating back harms the hater too, and that Black and white Americans can only be free together.
- [The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-immortal-life-of-henrietta-lacks/) by Rebecca Skloot: In 1951 doctors took cells from a poor Black woman without telling her, and those cells became one of the most useful tools in medicine, while her family was never told.
- [The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-man-who-mistook-his-wife-for-a-hat/) by Oliver Sacks: A brain illness is never only something taken away: the person inside keeps working to stay themselves, so to understand a patient you need their story, not just a list of what is wrong.
- [The Sum of Us](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-sum-of-us/) by Heather McGhee: The belief that one group gains only when another loses is a false story, and it has drained the shared goods that most Americans depend on.
- [Why Does He Do That?](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/why-does-he-do-that/) by Lundy Bancroft: Abuse comes from a man's attitudes of ownership and entitlement, not from his feelings, so a partner cannot fix him by understanding him or by being easier to live with.
- [Surely You’re Joking, Mr. Feynman!](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/surely-youre-joking-mr-feynman/) by Richard P. Feynman: Real understanding is something you test for yourself, with puzzles, plain examples, play and honesty, never with names, titles or the word of experts.
- [Dopamine Detox](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/dopamine-detox/) by Thibaut Meurisse: Constant stimulation makes your important work feel dull. Lower the noise, and hard things get easier to start.
- [How to Talk to Anyone](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/how-to-talk-to-anyone/) by Leil Lowndes: Success with people comes from small moves you can learn, and every one of them aims at the same thing: making the other person feel special and at ease.
- [Rich Dad Poor Dad](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/rich-dad-poor-dad-what-the-rich-teach-their-kids-about-money/) by Robert Kiyosaki: Wealth comes from financial education, not from a big paycheck: learn the difference between an asset and a liability, keep buying assets that put money in your pocket, and stay calm about the risk of losing.
- [The 48 Laws of Power](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-48-laws-of-power/) by Robert Greene: Power is a game that everyone plays, and Greene says you do better when you see how it works: keep a calm face, hide your aims, manage your image, learn what people want, stop in time, and stay hard to pin down.
- [The 5 AM Club](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-5-am-club/) by Robin Sharma: Get up at 5 AM and spend the first hour on yourself in three parts, move, reflect and grow, and keep it up for 66 days until it is automatic, while you guard your focus and your rest.
- [The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-7-habits-of-highly-effective-people/) by Stephen R. Covey: Lasting change works from the inside out: change how you see things, then build seven habits that take you from depending on others, to standing on your own, to working well with others.
- [What the Most Successful People Do Before Breakfast](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/what-the-most-successful-people-do-before-breakfast/) by Laura Vanderkam: The most successful people spend their early mornings, their weekends and their work hours on purpose, so what matters most gets done first.
- [How To Make Sh*t Happen](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/how-to-make-sh-t-happen/) by Sean Whalen: Everything you do in a day fits four areas: your body, the people in your life, your mind and your work. Give each one a planned action every day, and the chaos turns into results.
- [How to Win Friends and Influence People in the Digital Age](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/how-to-win-friends-influence-people-in-digital-age/) by Dale Carnegie & Associates: Carnegie's old rules still work online: you win friends and influence people by leaving each one a little better, and that starts with real interest in them.
- [The 80/20 Principle](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-80-20-principle/) by Richard Koch: A few causes make most of the results. Find your few, give them more, and give the rest less, at work and in life.
- [The Art of Seduction](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-art-of-seduction/) by Robert Greene: Seduction is a game of the mind, not of looks. A seducer builds a strong character, learns what the other person lacks, and leads them slowly into a spell.
- [Unf*ck Yourself](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/unf-k-yourself/) by Gary John Bishop: What you tell yourself shapes your life. So say seven strong sentences in the present, and then act, whatever you feel.
- [Deep Work](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/deep-work/) by Cal Newport: The power to focus without distraction on hard work is getting rarer and worth more every year, so people who build their work life around it will thrive.
- [No Excuses](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/no-excuses/) by Brian Tracy: Self-discipline, doing the right thing at the right time even when you do not feel like it, is the one skill that makes every other success rule work, and anyone can build it as a habit.
- [Read People Like a Book](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/read-people-like-a-book/) by Patrick King: You cannot see inside another person, so reading people means making careful guesses from many small clues, never trusting one sure sign.
- [The Power of Your Subconscious Mind](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-power-of-your-subconscious-mind/) by Joseph Murphy: Murphy says your deeper mind (the part of you that works below your attention) carries out whatever you deeply believe, so choose your thoughts, picture what you want as done, and hand it over calmly.
- [The Psychology of Money](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-psychology-of-money/) by Morgan Housel: How you behave with money matters much more than how much you know about it.
- [The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-subtle-art-of-not-giving-a-f-ck/) by Mark Manson: A good life does not come from caring about more and feeling good all the time. It comes from choosing the few things worth caring about, and accepting the pain that comes with them.
- [Think and Grow Rich!](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/think-and-grow-rich/) by Napoleon Hill: Napoleon Hill says every achievement starts as an idea. A burning goal, a written plan, quick decisions, steady effort and a few helpers turn it into real results.
- [Emotional Intelligence](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/emotional-intelligence1/) by Daniel Goleman: Feelings can swamp your thinking, or they can guide it. Goleman says five skills decide which one happens, and that these skills can matter as much as IQ, and sometimes more.
- [Money Master the Game](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/money-master-the-game/) by Tony Robbins: Anyone can build an income for life: decide how much of every paycheck you keep, avoid the hidden costs, and follow seven simple steps in order.
- [Talking to Strangers](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/talking-to-strangers/) by Malcolm Gladwell: We misread strangers because we start by believing them, trust faces and manner that do not show feelings, and ignore the setting, so we should meet them with caution and humility.
- [The Book You Wish Your Parents Had Read](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-book-you-wish-your-parents-had-read-and-your-children-will-be-glad-that-you-did/) by Philippa Perry: A child grows in the relationship with a parent, the way a plant grows in soil, so that relationship is the core of parenting.
- [The Power of Now](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-power-of-now/) by Eckhart Tolle: You are not your mind. The endless thinking in your head, and the old pain it feeds on, cause most of your suffering, and you end it by watching them and giving this moment your full attention.
- [Why We Sleep](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/why-we-sleep/) by Matthew Walker: Sleep is not one favor but many: each night it saves your memories, calms your feelings and protects your body, and Walker says we are losing too much of it.
- [Love Yourself Like Your Life Depends on It](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/love-yourself-like-your-life-depends-on-it/) by Kamal Ravikant: Make a vow to love yourself, then repeat “I love myself” every day with feeling, until your thoughts, and then your life, follow.
- [The ONE Thing](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-one-thing/) by Gary Keller, Jay Papasan: Big results come from going small: find the ONE Thing that makes everything else easier or unnecessary, and do it first.
- [Don’t Overthink It](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/don-t-overthink-it/) by Anne Bogel: Overthinking eats the hours of your life. You can win them back with small shifts: aim for good enough, decide once, and say yes to what you love.
- [Drama Free](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/drama-free/) by Nedra Glover Tawwab: You cannot change your family, but you can change how you take part in it, and that is enough to keep a hard relationship on your terms or to end it.
- [How to Be an Adult in Relationships](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/how-to-be-an-adult-in-relationships/) by David Richo: Love is five things: attention, acceptance, appreciation, affection and allowing. Being an adult in love means giving them and asking for them, even when your past, your fears and your ego get in the way.
- [Influence](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/influence/) by Robert B. Cialdini: Most of our yes decisions come from a few mental shortcuts. Each shortcut usually points the right way, and each can be used on us by someone who wants a yes.
- [My Age of Anxiety](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/my-age-of-anxiety/) by Scott Stossel: Anxiety is fear of something that has not happened yet. It grows from body, mind, genes, childhood and stress, so no single cure covers it.
- [The Science of Self-Discipline](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-science-of-self-discipline/) by Peter Hollins: Self-discipline is a skill you can train, and it works best when you also shape your surroundings, your people and your habits so that you need less willpower.
- [Biohack Your Brain](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/biohack-your-brain/) by Kristen Willeumier: At any age, you can improve your brain with everyday habits: moving, eating well, drinking water, calming stress, thinking kindly and learning new things.
- [Lives of the Stoics](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/lives-of-the-stoics/) by Ryan Holiday, Stephen Hanselman: The Stoics were judged by what they did, not what they said, and their lives and deaths show how to live well: with four virtues, a calm focus on what you control, and daily practice.
- [Million Dollar Habits](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/million-dollar-habits/) by Stellan Moreira: Your life follows your habits, so build the habits of a calm, happy mind first, then the habits that grow your money.
- [Mindful Relationship Habits](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/mindful-relationship-habits/) by Barrie Davenport, S.J. Scott: Love fades mostly from lack of attention, and a couple can bring it back by choosing small, mindful habits, one at a time.
- [Principles](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/principles/) by Ray Dalio: You get what you want by facing what is true, learning from your mistakes, and deciding together with the smartest people who disagree with you.
- [Why Has Nobody Told Me This Before?](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/why-has-nobody-told-me-this-before/) by Dr. Julie Smith: Your feelings are built from your thoughts, your body and your actions, so you have more power over them than you were taught, and a few simple tools put that power to use.
- [Presence](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/presence/) by Amy Cuddy: Presence is being able to show your real self in the moments that scare you. It comes from feeling personally powerful, and small nudges, in your mind and your body, can help you find it.
- [The 15 Invaluable Laws of Growth](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-15-invaluable-laws-of-growth/) by John C. Maxwell: You reach your potential by growing on purpose, every day, and fifteen laws show you how.
- [The Code of the Extraordinary Mind](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-code-of-the-extraordinary-mind/) by Vishen Lakhiani: Many of the rules you live by were handed to you, not chosen. Question them, pick your own beliefs and habits, and be happy now while a bold vision pulls you forward.
- [You Are a Badass at Making Money](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/you-are-a-badass-at-making-money/) by Jen Sincero: Sincero argues that old beliefs about money hold your income down, so you change the beliefs, get clear on why you want more, and act on what scares you.
- [You’re Not Listening](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/you-re-not-listening/) by Kate Murphy: People long to be heard, but most of us have stopped really listening. Good listening means being curious about what is in another person’s mind, and it is a skill you can build.
- [Make Your Bed](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/make-your-bed/) by William H. McRaven: Small habits, good teammates, courage and never quitting can change your life, and one person at a time, they can change the world.
- [The 5 Love Languages](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-5-love-languages/) by Gary Chapman: Love lasts when you learn which of five love languages your spouse understands best, and you choose to speak it.
- [Talk Like TED](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/talk-like-ted/) by Carmine Gallo: The talks people love reach the heart first, then give a fresh idea in a way people can see, feel and remember, in the speaker's own voice.
- [Tiny Habits](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/tiny-habits/) by BJ Fogg: BJ Fogg says that failing to change is a design flaw, not a flaw in you: pick a tiny behavior you already want, tie it to something you already do, and celebrate it right away.
- [Declutter Your Mind](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/declutter-your-mind/) by S. J. Scott, Barrie Davenport: You cannot stop thoughts from coming, but you can learn to watch them, answer them, and clear what feeds them.
- [Hold Me Tight](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/hold-me-tight/) by Sue Johnson: Adult love is a need for one safe person, so most fights are cries that ask are you there for me, and love lasts when partners learn to ask that clearly and answer with care.
- [How to Make People Like You in 90 Seconds or Less](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/how-to-make-people-like-you-in-90-seconds-or-less/) by Nicholas Boothman: People like people who are like them, so you can build rapport fast: pick a warm attitude, greet openly, match their body and voice, ask open questions and listen.
- [I Will Teach You to Be Rich](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/i-will-teach-you-to-be-rich/) by Ramit Sethi: You get rich by getting a few big things right once, then letting automatic, low-cost investing do the rest.
- [Power Questions](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/power-questions/) by Andrew Sobel, Jerold Panas: The right question at the right moment can do more than any answer: it builds trust, wins business and moves people.
- [Pre-Suasion](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/pre-suasion/) by Robert Cialdini: Before you ask for a yes, steer what the other person is thinking about. That moment can matter more than the ask itself.
- [The Charisma Myth](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-charisma-myth/) by Olivia Fox Cabane: Charisma is not a gift you are born with. It is behavior that shows presence, power and warmth, and anyone can learn it by starting inside.
- [The Diary of a CEO](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-diary-of-a-ceo/) by Steven Bartlett: Great things are built by people who follow a few lasting laws about themselves, their story, their thinking and their team.
- [The Miracle Morning](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-miracle-morning/) by Hal Elrod: Your success rises only as far as you do, so give the first hour of each day to six simple practices that build the person you want to be.
- [Words That Change Minds](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/words-that-change-minds/) by Shelle Rose Charvet: How a person talks shows what moves them. Ask a few questions, hear the pattern, and use words that match it.
- [8 Rules of Love](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/8-rules-of-love/) by Jay Shetty: Love is not a prize you find. It is a skill you practice every day: first with yourself, then with a partner, through hard times, and with everyone.
- [A Short History of Nearly Everything](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/a-short-history-of-nearly-everything/) by Bill Bryson: We know the story of the universe, the Earth and life because people kept asking "how do they know that?", and the answer shows how lucky we are to be here.
- [Active Listening Techniques](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/active-listening-techniques/) by Nixaly Leonardo: People listen to you when they feel heard, so start by listening with your whole self.
- [Calling in “The One”](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/calling-in-the-one-revised-and-expanded/) by Katherine Woodward Thomas: Searching harder for the right person will not change your love life. Becoming someone a great love can grow with will.
- [Digital Minimalism](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/digital-minimalism/) by Cal Newport: Use technology only for the few things you value most, and be happy to miss out on the rest.
- [How to Be Alone](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/how-to-be-alone/) by Lane Moore: When a home was never safe, you can feel alone in a crowd. The way through is to care for yourself, let kind people in, and say what you need.
- [How to Talk So Kids Will Listen & Listen So Kids Will Talk](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/how-to-talk-so-kids-will-listen-listen-so-kids-will-talk/) by Adele Faber, Elaine Mazlish: Children listen, cooperate and grow when you accept their feelings and talk without blame, so their self-respect stays whole.
- [Just Listen](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/just-listen-discover-the-secret-to-getting-through-to-absolutely-anyone/) by Mark Goulston: To get through to someone, get them talking. Say the feeling they are hiding, listen, and they start to say yes.
- [Negotiation Hacks](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/negotiation-hacks/) by Simon Rycraft: Negotiating well is six habits anyone can learn, built on preparation and trust, not on tricks.
- [Never Split the Difference](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/never-split-the-difference/) by Chris Voss, Tahl Raz: People decide with feelings, not logic, so listen until the other side feels understood, then guide them with questions.
- [Nexus](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/nexus-a-brief-history-of-information-networks-from-the-stone-age-to-ai/) by Yuval Noah Harari: Information does not mainly show us the truth. It connects people into networks, so every network needs ways to fix its own mistakes, and AI is the first member of those networks that is not human.
- [Sapiens](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/sapiens/) by Yuval Noah Harari: Humans rule the world because we can believe in shared stories, and those stories let millions of strangers work together.
- [Single On Purpose](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/single-on-purpose/) by John Kim: You cannot build a healthy bond with anyone until you build one with yourself, so use your single time, and your time inside a relationship, to know who you are.
- [Stop Checking Your Likes](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/stop-checking-your-likes/) by Susie Moore: You do not need anyone's approval to live the life you want, so stop waiting for it and give it to yourself.
- [The 10X Rule](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-10x-rule/) by Grant Cardone: Set your goals ten times higher than feels reasonable, then take ten times the action you think they need.
- [The Whole-Brain Child](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-whole-brain-child/) by Daniel J. Siegel and Tina Payne Bryson: A hard moment with your child is a chance to help the parts of their brain work together.
- [$100M Offers](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/100m-offers/) by Alex Hormozi: People pay for value, not for cost: build an offer worth far more than its price, and buyers stop comparing and start saying yes.
- [Cues](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/cues/) by Vanessa Van Edwards: People judge you on warmth and competence, and they read both from tiny signals called cues. You can learn to read them and to send them on purpose.
- [Dopamine Nation](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/dopamine-nation/) by Anna Lembke: Pleasure and pain sit on one balance in your brain, so chasing pleasure and running from pain tip it toward pain, and you can reset it.
- [How to Be Your Own Therapist](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/how-to-be-your-own-therapist/) by Owen O’Kane: You can learn the skills a therapist teaches, and use them yourself for ten minutes a day to feel steadier.
- [How to Break Up with Your Phone](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/how-to-break-up-with-your-phone/) by Catherine Price: Phones are built to hook your attention, so willpower alone is not enough. A 30-day plan can let you keep what you love about your phone and decide for yourself what gets your attention.
- [How to Get On with Anyone](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/how-to-get-on-with-anyone/) by Catherine Stothart: People deal with others in one of four styles, each driven by a different need, so read their style, adjust your own, and you can get on with anyone.
- [How to Know a Person](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/how-to-know-a-person/) by David Brooks: The skill under every good relationship is seeing another person deeply and making them feel seen. It can be learned.
- [How to Stop Losing Your Sh*t with Your Kids](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/how-to-stop-losing-your-shit-with-your-kids/) by Carla Naumburg: You lose your temper when a tired, overloaded nervous system gets pushed, so take care of yourself first, and when your kids push anyway, notice, pause and do anything else.
- [Leaders Eat Last](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/leaders-eat-last/) by Simon Sinek: People give their best when they feel safe with each other, and a leader's job is to build that safety, even when it costs the leader something.
- [Love Unfu*ked](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/love-unfu-ked/) by Gary John Bishop: A good relationship does not come from the right partner. You build it by managing yourself and keeping your word.
- [Meditations](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/meditations/) by Marcus Aurelius: You cannot control what happens, only what you think and do, so judge calmly, treat people kindly and do your work now.
- [Modern Romance](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/modern-romance/) by Aziz Ansari, Eric Klinenberg: Today we search for a soul mate through screens and endless options, so finding love takes more care: treat people as people, not as bubbles on a screen, and give them real time.
- [No-Drama Discipline](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/no-drama-discipline/) by Daniel J. Siegel and Tina Payne Bryson: Discipline means to teach. When a child misbehaves, connect first so the child can listen, then redirect toward a better choice.
- [Reasons to Stay Alive](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/reasons-to-stay-alive/) by Matt Haig: Depression is a real illness that lies about the future, and Matt Haig shows that small steps, other people and honest talk can lead back to life.
- [Scaling Up Excellence](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/scaling-up-excellence/) by Robert I. Sutton and Huggy Rao: Spreading excellence from a few people to many is slow, hands-on work, done one person and one small change at a time.
- [Scrum](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/scrum1/) by Jeff Sutherland: A plan made in advance is only a guess, so Scrum works in short cycles, ends each one with finished work, and fixes whatever slows the team down.
- [Set Boundaries, Find Peace](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/set-boundaries-find-peace/) by Nedra Glover Tawwab: A boundary is a need you say out loud and then back up with action, and the short discomfort of doing it is worth the peace you get.
- [Speed Reading](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/speed-reading/) by Kam Knight: Reading faster is a matter of changing a few habits: prepare first, take in groups of words, keep the inner voice quiet and never go back, then make sure you remember.
- [Start with Why](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/start-with-why/) by Simon Sinek: Buyers choose the reason behind what you do, so great leaders start with their purpose and work outward.
- [Stolen Focus](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/stolen-focus-why-you-cant-pay-attention/) by Johann Hari: Hari argues that our focus is falling apart because of twelve forces in the way we live, so fixing it takes personal steps and changes we make together.
- [Ten Arguments to Delete Your Social Media Account Right Now](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/ten-arguments-to-delete-your-social-media-account-right-now/) by Jaron Lanier: Social media earns its money by changing what you do for customers you cannot see, so Lanier argues you should delete your accounts and find out who you are without them.
- [The 11 Laws of Likability](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-11-laws-of-likability/) by Michelle Tillis Lederman: People do business with people they like, so build real connections instead of working a room: be yourself, be curious, give first and be patient.
- [The 2-Hour Job Search](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-2-hour-job-search-using-technology-to-get-the-right-job-faster/) by Steve Dalton: Online applications pile up unread, so jobs go to people who have someone inside speaking for them.
- [The 4-Hour Body](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-4-hour-body/) by Timothy Ferriss: Big changes in your body come from the smallest steps that work, tracked with numbers and tested on yourself.
- [The 4-Hour Workweek](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-4-hour-workweek/) by Timothy Ferriss: You do not need a million dollars or a retirement party to live freely: free your time and your place first, in four steps called DEAL.
- [The 5 Love Languages of Children](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-5-love-languages-of-children/) by Gary Chapman, Ross Campbell: Your child needs to feel your love, not only to have it, and you can fill that need by speaking the love language she understands best.
- [The 5 Second Rule](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-5-second-rule/) by Mel Robbins: When you feel an urge to act on a goal, count 5-4-3-2-1 and move before your brain stops you: change is made of these five-second acts of everyday courage.
- [The 7 Habits of Highly Effective Families](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-7-habits-of-highly-effective-families/) by Stephen R. Covey: Every family is off track most of the time; the strong ones know where they are going, change themselves first, and keep coming back.
- [The 80/20 CEO](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-80-20-ceo/) by Bill Canady: A business gets stronger when its leaders find the small share of customers and products that bring most of the profit, put their effort there, and run a simple hundred-day system to get started.
- [The Anxious Generation](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-anxious-generation/) by Jonathan Haidt: Jonathan Haidt argues that children born after 1995 grew up anxious because adults overprotected them in the real world and underprotected them online.
- [The Art of Reading Minds](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-art-of-reading-minds/) by Henrik Fexeus: People show much of what they think and feel in their body, face and voice, often without knowing it. If you notice it and adapt to it, you understand people better and they follow you more easily.
- [The Art of War](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-art-of-war/) by Sun Tzu: The best win costs the least: you prepare, you learn what the enemy will do, and you win before the fight starts, or without a fight at all.
- [The Automatic Millionaire](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-automatic-millionaire-expanded-and-updated/) by David Bach: You can get rich on an ordinary income if you pay yourself first and make every money move automatic.
- [The Danish Way of Parenting](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-danish-way-of-parenting/) by Jessica Joelle Alexander, Iben Dissing Sandahl: The authors say Danes top the world's happiness lists because of how they raise their children, and that six tools, which spell PARENT, work in any family.
- [The Great CEO Within](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-great-ceo-within/) by Matt Mochary: A great CEO is trained, not born: fix your own habits first, then run a simple written system that keeps a growing team pointed the same way.
- [The Let Them Theory](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-let-them-theory-a-life-changing-tool-that-millions-of-people-can-t-stop-talking-about/) by Mel Robbins: You cannot control other people, so say Let Them to let go of them, then say Let Me to choose what you do next.
- [The Pomodoro Technique](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/the-pomodoro-technique/) by Francesco Cirillo: Work in 25-minute boxes with real breaks, and time stops being an enemy and becomes a tool you can measure and improve.
- [Unlimited Memory](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/unlimited-memory/) by Kevin Horsley: A good memory is a skill, not a gift: pay full attention, turn what you want to keep into a silly moving picture, hang it on a place you already know, and review it.
- [21 Lessons for the 21st Century](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/21-lessons-for-the-21st-century/) by Yuval Noah Harari: The big stories that explained the world are failing just as new technology arrives, so the best defense is to see through stories, admit what you do not know, and know your own mind.
- [Refactoring UI](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/refactoring-ui/) by Adam Wathan, Steve Schoger: A good-looking interface needs no artistic talent: build one real feature at a time, choose from short lists of values, and make what matters stand out.
- [13 Things Mentally Strong People Don't Do](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/13-things-mentally-strong-people-don-t-do/) by Amy Morin: You are only as strong as your worst habits, so mental strength means dropping thirteen habits of thinking, feeling and acting that hold you back.
- [How to Stop Worrying And Start Living](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/summaries/how-to-stop-worrying-and-start-living/) by Dale Carnegie: Worry wears down your body and clouds your mind, but you can break the habit by living one day at a time, facing the worst with clear facts, and choosing calm action.

## Courses

- [Justice](https://bookmuse.wanngo.com/courses/justice/): 10 parts. Ten short parts on the big question of what is fair: making the most people happy, owning ourselves, what money shouldn't buy, doing right for its own sake, choosing rules behind a veil, who deserves what, and the ties we never chose. Each part uses everyday cases.
